publishFields.title: AI Systems Atlas – Open-source exploration of Markdown documents as a source-grounded 3D knowledge graph
publishFields.body:
AI Systems Atlas is a local-first knowledge graph web app that parses README and development-plan Markdown files into nodes and relationships, then lets you explore them with source evidence in a Three.js graph.

As README files and development plans accumulated during the project, searching files one by one made it difficult to understand how concepts and tasks were connected. I built a graph that extracts the Markdown document structure and explicitly stated relationships for direct exploration.

AI Systems Atlas parses Markdown with a Remark AST and represents documents, sections, concepts, phases, and tasks as nodes. Structural and explicit relationships retain their source paths, and the browser interface provides constellation, nebula, and selected-node orbit views.

The public demo opens without login. It is a read-only static version without a production database or OAuth connection, where you can try search, filters, zoom, rotation, and node-relationship exploration.

- Public demo: https://ai-systems-atlas.vercel.app/?scope=corpus&view=constellation
- GitHub: https://github.com/coreline-ai/memory_node_graph
- License: MIT
- Core technologies: TypeScript, React, Three.js

The project is currently an active prototype. The public demo is a read-only version that displays only a verified static snapshot.

Is the distinction between source-grounded relationships and layout-only connections clear on the first screen? When exploring a node, which source details would you want to see first?

publishFields.title: I built AI Systems Atlas and would like feedback on the first-use flow
publishFields.body:
As my document collection grew, I kept losing sight of the connections between files, so I built AI Systems Atlas: a web app for exploring Markdown documents as a relational knowledge graph.

It displays links between documents as a graph. I made the hard decision to leave out editing and open a read-only public demo first.

Built with TypeScript, React, and Three.js. Licensed under MIT.

Repository: https://github.com/coreline-ai/memory_node_graph
Demo: https://ai-systems-atlas.vercel.app/?scope=corpus&view=constellation

What, if anything, feels confusing when you first open the demo?

summary.oneSentence: AI Systems Atlas is a web app for exploring Markdown documents as a relational knowledge graph.
summary.shortIntro: As my document collection grew, I kept losing sight of the connections between files, so I built a graph explorer.
features: Displays links between documents as a graph.
